classification.rationale: procd is PID 1. Its failure mode is a device reboot and there is no in-band recovery. It also owns the service, system and hotplug object families that every other responsibility depends on.
classification.recovery_constraint: No in-band recovery exists; only the bootloader or a power cycle.
run: Q06 service list: 19 services, instance and trigger state matches the static graph
src: procd state machine and inittab handler pinned at 58eb263d

classification.rationale: The init framework is shell that procd interprets by convention. Replacing it means reimplementing procd's expectations without changing procd, which buys nothing until a specific service is replaced.
run: Q06: reload semantics per service confirmed by which services expose reload_service
src: rc.common dispatch table read in full

dep: 21 preinit hook files; inittab with 3 entries
classification.rationale: Boot orchestration decides whether the device boots at all. A failure here is recoverable only through failsafe or the bootloader, and this project has no recovery gate.
classification.recovery_constraint: Failsafe or TFTP/bootloader recovery only; needs physical access.
run: Q01 kernel cmdline has no rootfs_mount_options.*; Q02 failsafe not entered

dep: 6 shipped configs; /etc/config content and hashes observed
classification.rationale: UCI is a plausible Rust target and its format is small, but the binding constraint is unknown-field preservation on read-modify-write across three concurrent writer families (shell, ucode, C) with no cross-process lock. That cannot be settled by observation; it needs a differential experiment, which is a C1/V1 activity.
run: Q12: no uncommitted delta at observation time; Q13: 4 of 6 shipped configs drifted

classification.rationale: reload_config is 17 lines of shell whose own upstream comment calls it a temporary hack until configd exists. Its static surface is narrow and its runtime baseline and trigger registrations are observed: compare normalised uci show output per package against a tmpfs md5 baseline and emit one config.change event per differing package. Delivery itself still needs the RK-01 oracle before C1 can freeze the contract. Its failure mode is silent, which is exactly the class of defect a typed implementation removes. It has no persistent state beyond a regenerable baseline, so a wrong version is recoverable by deleting that file.
run: Q12: /var/run/config.md5 baseline observed with its tracked package list
Q06: config.change triggers observed on the consuming services
src: base-files recipe; upstream comment naming it a temporary hack

classification.rationale: First-boot generation runs once and depends on MTD-sourced MAC values for this board. Its blast radius is a device with no network configuration, and it is not on any hot path afterwards. There is no operational gain from rewriting it.
run: Q03: /etc/uci-defaults empty and board.json present, so generation already ran

classification.rationale: netifd is the largest single control-plane surface: 3 base objects plus one object per interface, its own protocol handler contract, and a ucode wireless sub-API. The interface is now fully catalogued and verified against runtime, but a replacement would have to reproduce the proto handler and wireless notify contracts, neither of which has been exercised.
run: Q05 and Q07: 4 interfaces, 9 devices, method signatures captured
src: netifd pinned at cbb83a18; ubus.c object tables parsed

classification.rationale: Wireless spans hostapd, wpa_supplicant, a ucode layer and mt76 driver behaviour. The project's non-goals exclude rewriting drivers and mature execution-plane components, and a wireless fault is not remotely recoverable on a device administered over its own LAN.
classification.recovery_constraint: A wireless fault can remove the only administrative path for a wireless-only client.
run: Q11: wpad runs as uid 101 with capabilities but no namespace isolation
src: hostap pinned at ca266cc2; ubus support is patch plus ucode

dep: /sbin/fw4 is present in the exact image
classification.rationale: firewall4 is already ucode rather than C, is one-shot, and its entire output is an nftables ruleset that can be diffed. That makes it unusually testable. But its compatibility contract is the generated ruleset, and no differential comparison has been run yet, so it cannot move further than defer.
run: Q08: table inet fw4 captured with 28 chains and one flowtable

classification.rationale: dnsmasq is a mature execution-plane daemon serving DNS and DHCPv4 for every client. The project explicitly preserves such components. Its ubus surface is one method.
run: Q09: object registered under the default name with only the metrics method
src: dnsmasq 2.93 verified against PKG_HASH; ubus object via upstream plus patch

dep: /usr/sbin/odhcpd and odhcp6c; dhcp and odhcp6c.wan objects observed
classification.rationale: odhcpd and odhcp6c are execution-plane IPv6 daemons. Same reasoning as R10, and this build is the reduced ipv6only variant with a three-method surface.
run: Q09: dhcp has no ipv4leases, confirming the ipv6only build

classification.rationale: ubusd is the transport every other responsibility uses. It has no persistent state, but restarting it drops every registered object and forces every daemon to reconnect. Replacing the bus before any client is replaced inverts the dependency order.
classification.recovery_constraint: A restart loses all 40 registered objects at once; recovery depends on every daemon reconnecting.
run: Q05: 40 objects; Q06: ubus supervised as a procd service with user ubus
src: ubus pinned at 24864e78; umask 0111 giving a 0666 socket

dep: /sbin/rpcd plus 6 plugins; 9 ACL files; session timeout 30 observed
classification.rationale: rpcd is the remote-administration boundary and, through file.exec and rc.init, is equivalent to remote code execution. Its ACL model is per-method and its session semantics are observable. The useful first move is not to replace it but to put a typed Rust layer in front of the ACL and session decision, where a mistake is contained and auditable. A full replacement would have to reproduce nine object families that LuCI depends on by exact field name.
run: Q05: full method signatures for session, uci, rc, file, rpc-sys, luci-rpc
Q13: rpcd config unchanged from the image; login scope is read/write '*'
src: rpcd pinned at 28faf640; per-method ACL evaluation read

dep: /usr/sbin/uhttpd; listens on :80 and :443 v4 and v6
classification.rationale: uhttpd runs as root and terminates TLS on all interfaces. It is a credible Rust target on memory-safety grounds alone, but its LuCI coupling runs through lua_prefix and ubus_prefix handlers that have not been exercised, and no differential test exists.
run: Q13: ubus_prefix /ubus, no_ubusauth unset, ubus_cors unset

dep: /sbin/logd; log object with read and write
classification.rationale: logd has a two-method surface and a failure mode confined to observability. That makes it the lowest-risk place to prove the ubus object, ACL and procd instance contracts end to end. Wrapping, not replacing, because the ring buffer is already the mechanism that made boot evidence unavailable and a rewrite should not start by changing retention semantics.
run: Q11: runs as uid 514
Q06: 1 of 3 declared instances active
Q02: ring buffer covers about 93 minutes
src: ubox pinned at 6f78fa49; in-process getpwnam drop

classification.rationale: hotplug dispatch is procd-internal plus 10 shell handlers. It cannot be separated from R01 without replacing procd, and a missed event is never retried, so the failure mode is silent and unrecoverable.
run: Q05: 10 hotplug subsystems, against 4 inferable from the ACL alone

classification.rationale: sysupgrade, factory and reboot are terminal. A defect here bricks the device. The project reserves this as the recovery gate and has no authorization to exercise it.
classification.recovery_constraint: A failed sysupgrade requires bootloader recovery and physical access.
run: Q00 and Q14: identity and package set confirmed; no terminal method exercised
src: procd system.c and rpcd sys.c pinned

risks.detail: R05's failure mode is a missed event; the service keeps running stale config and nothing reports an error.
risks.evidence: reload_config read in full; whole-file md5 granularity; tmpfs baseline
risks.mitigation: Any replacement must make delivery observable before it changes detection.

risks.detail: wpad declares procd_add_jail but gets no namespace isolation, because the call passes a name with no flags or mounts.
risks.mitigation: Treat the declaration and the observed namespace set as separate facts in any design.
risks.risk: Declared isolation is not effective isolation

risks.detail: Both ACL layers authorise absent objects: udebug in the ubusd layer, dsl and fingerprint in the rpcd layer.
risks.evidence: Q10 udebug Not found; rpcd ACL coverage check
risks.mitigation: Never treat an ACL as an interface inventory; it is an intent declaration.
risks.risk: ACL grants objects that do not exist

risks.detail: The historical DNS override is inactive and DHCP now matches expected first-boot semantics, but backup files remain in /etc/config and therefore remain visible to reload_config's all-file scan. Firewall software flow offloading is an active device-specific delta.
risks.mitigation: Use the reviewed current config and full observed /etc/config file set as the C1 fixture; never substitute image defaults.
risks.risk: Device carries configuration history from an earlier tool

risks.detail: The ubus catalog closes bidirectionally against one configuration; a STA interface or a log_file setting would create objects and instances never seen.
risks.evidence: wpa_supplicant.<ifname> has no instance; log has 1 of 3 declared instances
risks.mitigation: State the configuration scope alongside any completeness claim.
risks.risk: Static catalogs are complete only for the observed configuration

risks.detail: rc.init and file.exec execute arbitrary programs, gated only by rpcd session ACL, and the shipped login grants read/write '*'.
risks.evidence: Q05 method signatures; Q13 rpcd login scope
risks.mitigation: Any wrapper must preserve or tighten the ACL decision, never widen it.
risks.risk: Remote code execution paths are reachable by design

risks.detail: The default log buffer cannot hold a boot record, and default procd debug level 0 does not emit its per-script DEBUG(2) duration records.
risks.mitigation: Any boot-path work needs a serial console or instrumented lab boot arranged in advance.
